yad-ephraim.1#_: Matters where there is concern of prohibition. Baer Heitev; see Peri Megadim part 2 siman 116: one about whom rumor spread that he had several jugs of stam yeinam to sell to Jews while presumed kosher, and he says the stam yeinam in his hand he already sold to a gentile and it was kosher, and the gentiles contradict him and doubt fell on other wines he brought whether he is believed they were made kosher — ruled that since he was compelled by community decree and judges to clarify to whom he sold his yayin nesech and he says to gentiles in such-and-such village they seized and confessed on their word — we presume him a liar and do not rely on him until he swears a severe oath as the judge sees fit that he sold to those gentiles and all wines he brought into the community were made kosher per our Torah law; if he does not swear he remains suspected and the wine he brought is presumed stam yeinam; responsa Pri Chadash Yoreh Deah siman 14 on reliability of those suspected in prohibitions and many distinctions regarding habitual sinners for appetite in slaughter or other prohibitions.
yad-ephraim.2#_: Regarding other matters. Baer Heitev; responsa Masat Moshe Yoreh Deah siman 104: one who practices forbidding lighting his pipe from smoke called titun from a milk candle — forbidden to tell one who practices leniency to light his pipe from that candle unless he specifies not to light from a milk candle, since for himself he practices prohibition; there he inclined to permit one who practices leniency to light a milk candle to mislead one who practices prohibition by saying it is a wax candle, citing Maharalbach responsum 121 and Peri Chadash Orach Chaim 496 on customs of Ashkenaz; also proof from beginning of chapter HaIshah Shalom; Shach siman 119 brought Maharalbach; for practice it appears certainly forbidden to mislead with false speech; the proof can be rejected; I shortened.
yad-ephraim.3#_: Even under oath. Baer Heitev; responsa Pri Chadash Yoreh Deah siman 16: Jews who went from other lands to purify yayin nesech and some did for themselves and some for other Jews as hired workers; they testified these drank yayin nesech daily and when asked why they said it is pikuach nefesh because in those lands water is bad and causes stomach illness and there is no other drink — ruled this is only appetite, for we do not testify they denied this mitzvah entirely, for perhaps if kosher wine were before them they would drink; and though not clear, since we did not see them drink when permitted wine was before them we establish the man on his presumption as Choshen Mishpat siman 34 if we saw him tying or untying on Shabbat, etc.; responsa Mayim Rabim 24–26: those suspected on stam yeinam are not believed to make others' wine in purity; responsa Devar Shmuel 61; also copied a responsum from another who is stringent; the author inclined to leniency by oath if they impose and threaten to speak truth if any incident occurred during wine work or their hand slipped from supervision entrusted to them and we rely on what they say under oath; see Bei Chayei and Chokhmat Adam siman 188.
yad-ephraim.4#_: One who says. Responsa Tashbetz part 3 siman 83: cheese sent from the forced ones from those suspected of eating gentile cheeses — forbidden to eat, unlike Raah in Beit HaBehirah; he conceded to Ribash.
